samples.summary: Delta puts an unbounded `while (true)` parent walk on the per-keystroke path; a cyclic `blockParentMap` would hang the tab (availability only)
samples.evidence: `resolveNestedTableLayout` walks up `layout.blockParentMap` in an unterminated `while (true)` loop (table-layout.ts:344-348) with no visited-set and no depth cap; the second walk at lines 369-374 is bounded only by reaching `topTableId`. This delta newly routes `getVisualLineRange` — and therefore `getWrapAffinity`, which runs on every inserted character (text-editor.ts:4071) — through that resolver, so the loop now executes on each keystroke inside any table cell instead of only on the click/selection paths. Attack chain: a collaborator (or a corrupted/hand-crafted CRDT payload) that produces a `blockParentMap` where a table block is transitively its own ancestor makes the walk never terminate, freezing the editor's main thread — a denial of service with no recovery short of reloading. I could not complete the chain: `blockParentMap` is built by a downward traversal of the block tree in `editor.ts:1313` / `text-box-editor.ts:473`, and a Yorkie tree cannot legally contain itself, so I found no reachable way to actually create the cycle. Hardening only: bound the walk (visited set or max nesting depth) so hostile/inconsistent map data degrades instead of hanging.
